analogs.covers: Social life: huge chatty flocks roosting on ledges, strong but jealous pairs, clever navigators
Food: the inland-river gull that plucks fish, trails bigger animals for scraps and mobs in messy dives

headline: A huge, chatty pigeon flock of the inland rivers that eats like a gull: fish, stolen scraps and messy dive-bombing.

setting.label: Inland rivers, lakes and ponds
setting.note: Nomadic flocks travel inland along freshwater sources and move to a new spot most mornings. Poor night vision means the flock always roosts on ledges before dark. Courtship happens in the mountains and nesting at a big lake.

playsLike: You are a small daytime flier in an unlimited flock. Fish is your staple, and you'd rather scavenge from any claimed corpse, at your own risk, than hunt. When you do hunt, unlimited numbers dive-bomb Medium-or-smaller prey, unattended babies or anything on death scars, with frequent friendly fire. You pair deeply but jealously, keep a few friends, and hold grudges. You flee Hatzegopteryx and Quetzalcoatlus, avoid Tropeognathus, and bond with Torvosaurus packs as their lookouts.

why.text: Large flocks that always stop to roost on ledges before nightfall, the classic pigeon life (official inspiration: pigeons).
Recognises its own reflection and memorises successful routes to prey. Pigeons are master navigators with a remarkable memory for places and faces.
Strong pairbonds, with a very jealous, sulky reaction when a partner nests with someone else.
Plucks freshwater fish and trails Large and Apex carnivores to scavenge their kills, as black-headed gulls work inland rivers and follow the plough.
Hunts by repeatedly dive-bombing with plenty of accidental friendly fire, and harasses brightly coloured species just for fun.

notLike: Pigeons are vegetarians; Thalassodromeus is a carnivore that eats fish and scavenges.
twist: Its bond with Torvosaurus works like ravens and wolves: it warns its pack of rival Torvosaurus in exchange for scraps.
